## WhatsApp Catalog Setup for D2C Brands: Requirements, Process and Practical Checklist

WhatsApp catalog setup for D2C brands requires a verified or active WhatsApp Business account, accurate product information, good product images, pricing, stock details and a clear method for accepting orders and payments. The catalog can help customers browse products inside WhatsApp, but it does not automatically create a complete online store or payment system.

For Indian D2C brands, WhatsApp is often used alongside Instagram, a Shopify or WooCommerce website, marketplaces, payment links and courier platforms. A well-prepared WhatsApp catalog gives customers a shorter path from product discovery to enquiry, order confirmation and support.

This guide explains the requirements, setup choices, product data, compliance considerations and operational steps involved in creating a WhatsApp catalog.

## What a WhatsApp Catalog Does for a D2C Brand

A WhatsApp catalog is a product showcase available through the WhatsApp Business app or connected WhatsApp commerce tools. Customers can open the catalog from your business profile, browse products, view product details and send enquiries or product messages.

Depending on the account setup and available features, customers may also be able to:

- Add products to a cart
- Send a cart as a WhatsApp message
- Ask questions about a product
- Request sizes, colours or variants
- Open a website product page
- Use a payment link shared by the business
- Receive order and delivery updates

The catalog is particularly useful for products that require conversation before purchase. Examples include clothing, skincare, jewellery, food products, home décor, gifts, wellness products and custom-made items.

It is not a replacement for every part of an e-commerce system. WhatsApp Business may not manage your complete inventory, shipping rules, GST invoicing, returns, refunds or customer account system. Those processes need to be handled manually or connected through other software.

For a D2C brand, the catalog is best treated as a social commerce storefront and enquiry channel. It helps a customer move from an Instagram post, QR code, Google Business Profile or referral to a product conversation.

### Common use cases

A D2C brand may use a WhatsApp catalog to:

- Share a product range with customers who do not want to visit a website
- Send individual product links during an Instagram conversation
- Present a curated collection for a festival or campaign
- Let a reseller or sales representative share the same product list
- Answer product questions through WhatsApp chat
- Handle repeat orders from existing customers
- Share products in local communities or customer groups, where appropriate
- Support customers who prefer UPI, cash on delivery or direct assistance

The experience works best when the information in the catalog matches what the business can actually sell and deliver.

## Requirements Before WhatsApp Catalog Setup

Before you begin, collect the business and product information in one place. Entering products one by one without preparation often leads to inconsistent names, missing prices, poor images and outdated stock information.

### 1. A suitable WhatsApp Business account

You need a WhatsApp Business account rather than relying only on a personal WhatsApp account. The account should have:

- A dedicated business mobile number
- Business name and category
- Profile image or logo
- Business description
- Customer support hours
- Business email or website, where relevant
- A clear display name that customers can recognise

A separate number is usually better for a D2C brand than using a founder’s personal number. It makes handover, customer support and future integration easier.

If you plan to use WhatsApp Business Platform, also called the WhatsApp API by many providers, the requirements are different. You may need Meta Business verification, an approved display name, a business portfolio and a technology provider or platform for managing conversations.

### 2. Product information

Prepare a product master sheet before uploading the catalog. At minimum, record:

- Product name
- Short description
- Selling price
- Currency
- SKU or internal product code
- Available variants
- Size or quantity
- Colour or flavour, where applicable
- Stock status
- Product category
- Product image
- Website or checkout link
- Shipping notes
- Return or exchange conditions

For products with variants, decide how they will appear. You can list each important variant separately, or list one main product and explain the available options in the description. Separate listings are often clearer when prices differ by size, pack or quantity.

### 3. Product images

Product images should be clear, consistent and suitable for a mobile screen. A customer viewing the catalog may be using a low-cost phone or a slower mobile connection, so large files and cluttered images can reduce usability.

A practical image set may include:

- A clean main product image
- A close-up showing texture or material
- A side or back view
- A size or usage image
- Packaging, where it affects the buying decision
- A lifestyle image, if it helps explain use

Avoid placing important information only inside the image. Price, size, ingredients, offers and terms should also appear as text in the product details.

### 4. Business and tax information

The catalog itself may not require every legal detail, but your overall selling process should be prepared. Keep the following ready:

- Legal business name
- Brand name and registered address
- GST registration details, if applicable
- Customer care contact
- Return and refund policy
- Shipping policy
- Privacy policy
- Terms of sale
- FSSAI details for applicable food businesses
- Product-specific licences or declarations where required

GST treatment depends on the product, business structure, turnover, place of supply and selling model. Do not assume that a WhatsApp order is outside GST requirements. Confirm invoicing and tax treatment with your accountant or tax adviser.

## Choosing the Right WhatsApp Setup

There are two broad ways to use WhatsApp for a D2C catalog: the WhatsApp Business app and the WhatsApp Business Platform.

| Requirement | WhatsApp Business app | WhatsApp Business Platform |
|---|---|---|
| Suitable for | Small or early-stage D2C operations | Growing teams and structured customer support |
| Catalog management | Managed through the app, subject to available features | May use connected systems, providers or commerce tools |
| Number of support users | Limited and dependent on the app setup | Better suited to multiple agents through a support inbox |
| Automation | Basic greeting, away and quick replies | Templates, workflow automation and integrations |
| Order handling | Often manual through chat, cart and payment links | Can connect with CRM, store, helpdesk or order systems |
| Setup complexity | Lower | Higher and may involve verification, onboarding and technical work |
| Best use | Product browsing and direct conversations | Scaled support, notifications and sales workflows |

The WhatsApp Business app is generally sufficient if the brand has a small product range, one or a few support staff and a manageable order volume.

The Platform becomes more relevant when you need several agents, automated order messages, customer segmentation, abandoned-cart workflows, CRM integration, support tickets or connections with a website and order management system.

Do not move to the Platform only because it sounds more advanced. It introduces additional setup, message-template rules, provider costs and operational decisions. Start with the simplest system that your team can manage reliably.

### Catalog versus full e-commerce website

A catalog is useful when customers are comfortable asking questions and ordering through chat. A website is usually better when customers need:

- Many product filters
- Detailed variant selection
- Real-time stock information
- Automated shipping calculation
- Coupon codes
- Customer accounts
- Reviews and ratings
- Multiple payment options
- Automated invoices
- Returns and exchanges through a dashboard

Many D2C brands use both. WhatsApp supports conversation and repeat buying, while the website handles structured checkout and order management.

## Product Data Requirements for a High-Quality Catalog

Uploading products is only the first step. The details must help a customer make a decision without repeatedly asking basic questions.

### Product names

Use names that are easy to understand and search. Include the product type and the most important differentiator.

For example:

- Cotton Handblock Kurta – Indigo
- Cold-Pressed Groundnut Oil – 1 Litre
- Vitamin C Face Serum – 30 ml
- Personalised Gift Box – Medium

Avoid internal names such as “SKU 107” or creative campaign names that do not explain the product.

### Descriptions

A useful description should answer:

- What is the product?
- Who is it for?
- What does the customer receive?
- What are the size, quantity or dimensions?
- How is it used?
- What makes it different?
- Are there important exclusions or limitations?

Keep the opening lines clear because customers may not read a long block of text. Use simple language and avoid claims that cannot be supported.

For food, cosmetics and wellness products, be careful with health-related claims. Do not present a product as treating, curing or preventing a medical condition unless the claim is legally permitted and properly supported.

### Prices and offers

Display the actual selling price clearly. If you show a discount, the original price and offer conditions should be genuine and understandable.

Mention relevant details such as:

- Whether GST is included
- Whether shipping is extra
- Minimum order value
- Offer validity, if limited
- Pack size
- Subscription or repeat-order terms
- Customisation charges

If prices change often, assign a person to review the catalog regularly. An outdated price can create avoidable disputes, especially when customers rely on screenshots.

### Stock and availability

WhatsApp catalog information may not automatically match stock in your website or warehouse. If you do not have synchronisation, use operational labels such as:

- In stock
- Made to order
- Pre-order
- Limited availability
- Confirm availability before payment

Do not accept payment for a product that is not available unless the customer has clearly agreed to a waiting period or alternative.

## How to Set Up a WhatsApp Catalog

The exact menu names can change as Meta updates WhatsApp Business features. The general process remains similar.

### Step 1: Complete the business profile

Install or open WhatsApp Business and complete the profile. Add the brand name, logo, category, description, support hours, website and email where available.

Use the same business identity across your website, Instagram, packaging and payment pages. Inconsistent names can reduce customer confidence.

### Step 2: Open the catalog section

In WhatsApp Business, open the business tools area and locate the catalog option. Add products or services individually. The product form generally asks for:

- Product name
- Price
- Description
- Product code
- Website or checkout link
- Product images

Feature availability can vary by account, location, device and current Meta policies. If the catalog option is not visible, check that you are using the WhatsApp Business app, update the app and review the official help resources.

### Step 3: Upload and review images

Add the clearest image as the primary image. Check how it appears in the mobile preview. A product that looks good on a desktop may appear too small or cropped on a phone.

Use a consistent background and visual style where possible. Consistency makes a small catalog look more organised without requiring expensive photography.

### Step 4: Add complete product details

Enter the price, description, code and relevant link. If the item has a size chart, care instructions or ingredients, include the essential information in the description and link to the full page if necessary.

Do not copy website text that contains irrelevant internal information, technical jargon or long promotional claims.

### Step 5: Organise products into collections

Collections can group products by a customer’s shopping purpose rather than only by internal stock categories. Examples include:

- New arrivals
- Bestsellers
- Under a selected price range
- Festive gifting
- Office wear
- Skincare routine
- Hair care
- Combo packs
- Ready to ship
- Custom orders

Collections help customers browse a smaller, more relevant selection. Avoid creating too many collections with only one or two products unless the grouping has a clear purpose.

### Step 6: Test the customer journey

Use a separate phone or ask someone outside the business to test:

- Opening the business profile
- Viewing the catalog
- Opening a product
- Understanding the price
- Selecting or asking about a variant
- Sending a product or cart message
- Opening the website link
- Completing payment
- Receiving order confirmation
- Asking for cancellation or return information

This test often reveals unclear product names, broken links, missing shipping details or slow replies.

## Orders, Payments and Delivery

A WhatsApp catalog displays products, but the order process needs separate planning. Decide exactly what happens after a customer sends a product message or cart.

### Manual order flow

A simple manual process may look like this:

1. Customer sends a product or cart message.
2. Team confirms product, variant, quantity and availability.
3. Team calculates shipping and final amount.
4. Customer receives payment instructions or a payment link.
5. Business confirms payment or cash-on-delivery terms.
6. Order is entered into a spreadsheet, store or order system.
7. Invoice is prepared where applicable.
8. Shipment is booked through the chosen courier or shipping platform.
9. Customer receives dispatch and delivery updates.
10. After delivery, the team handles support, exchange or feedback.

This approach can work for a small order volume, but it depends on disciplined record-keeping.

### Payment options in India

Depending on your business model, you may accept:

- UPI
- Payment gateway links
- Debit or credit cards through a gateway
- Net banking
- Cash on delivery
- Bank transfer
- Website checkout

A payment link from a recognised payment gateway is generally easier to track than asking customers to send money to a personal account. Use a business bank account and retain transaction records.

Avoid sending sensitive payment information through chat. Do not ask customers for UPI PINs, card PINs, passwords or one-time passwords. A business should never need a customer’s UPI PIN to receive payment.

### Delivery and returns

Before accepting an order, make delivery terms visible. Customers should know:

- Serviceable locations
- Expected dispatch approach
- Shipping charges
- Cash-on-delivery availability
- Packaging conditions
- Exchange or return eligibility
- Damage reporting process
- Refund method and possible deductions

For perishable products, intimate apparel, customised items or hygiene-sensitive products, return conditions may differ. State them clearly and ensure they are consistent with applicable consumer protection requirements.

## India-Specific Compliance and Trust Requirements

A WhatsApp catalog is part of your customer-facing sales process, so the wider business must follow applicable Indian rules.

### Consumer information

Customers should be able to identify the seller and contact the business. Keep the business name, customer support route and relevant policy links easy to find.

The Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 may apply depending on how your business operates. Product information, pricing, grievance handling and refund practices should be reviewed for compliance with the rules relevant to your business.

### GST and invoices

Whether GST applies, how it is charged and what invoice is required depends on your registration status and transaction details. A catalog price should not create confusion about whether GST is included or added at checkout.

If your system is manual, create a standard invoice process. Make sure the invoice contains the information required for your business and tax situation. Ask a qualified tax professional if you sell across states, operate through multiple entities or use marketplaces.

### Privacy and customer data

Customer phone numbers, addresses, order histories and payment details are sensitive business information. Limit access to authorised staff and avoid keeping customer data indefinitely without a business reason.

If you connect WhatsApp to a CRM, spreadsheet, chatbot or third-party inbox, check how that provider stores and processes data. Your privacy policy should explain relevant data practices in plain language.

### Restricted products and claims

Meta has commerce policies and WhatsApp policies that restrict or limit certain products and content. Categories such as regulated health products, weapons, adult products, financial services and certain supplements may require special attention or may not be permitted.

Review current platform policies before investing in a catalog for a restricted category. Do not try to bypass restrictions by using misleading product names or images.

## Catalog Maintenance and Daily Operations

The catalog is not a one-time project. A product page becomes a customer promise, so it must remain accurate.

Create a simple maintenance routine.

### Weekly checks

Review:

- Prices
- Stock status
- Broken links
- Product images
- Collections
- Current offers
- Shipping information
- Frequently asked questions from customers

### Monthly checks

Review:

- Products that no longer sell
- Products with frequent support questions
- Outdated seasonal collections
- Return and exchange issues
- Response time during busy periods
- Catalog visits or product enquiries, if the available tools show them
- Repeated manual tasks that could be automated

### Assign ownership

Someone should own catalog accuracy. This might be the founder, store manager, marketing executive or customer support lead.

Define who can:

- Add a new product
- Change a price
- Mark an item unavailable
- Approve promotional copy
- Reply to customer enquiries
- Confirm refunds
- Update delivery information

Without ownership, a catalog can remain online even after a product, offer or policy has changed.

### Use saved replies carefully

Quick replies can save time for common questions about:

- Size charts
- Shipping
- Payment methods
- Return policy
- Care instructions
- Customisation
- Order status

They should be edited before sending when the customer’s order has a special condition. Automation should reduce repetitive work, not make responses feel careless.

## Common Mistakes D2C Brands Should Avoid

### Uploading every product at once

A large catalog is not automatically better. Start with the products that are in stock, profitable, easy to explain and suitable for WhatsApp conversations.

### Using incomplete descriptions

A customer should not need to ask for the pack size, material, ingredients or basic usage details. Missing information increases response workload and can cause wrong orders.

### Treating catalog price as final without explaining shipping

If shipping varies by location or order value, say so clearly. Unexpected delivery charges are a common reason for customers to abandon a purchase.

### Accepting orders without a tracking method

Record every order in a store system, spreadsheet or order management tool. Include customer name, phone number, product, variant, payment status, delivery address and fulfilment status.

### Sharing promotional messages without consent

Do not assume that because a person once ordered, they want every future campaign. Follow WhatsApp messaging rules and respect opt-outs. Promotional messaging through the WhatsApp Business Platform may also require approved templates and category-specific controls.

### Using misleading urgency

Statements such as “last piece” or “offer ends today” should be true. Trust is more valuable than a short-term conversion.

### Ignoring human support

A catalog can start a conversation, but customers may still need help with sizes, allergies, delivery areas, exchanges or customisation. Make sure a person can take over when needed.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is a WhatsApp catalog the same as an online store?

No. A catalog displays products and helps customers begin an enquiry or order conversation. It may not provide full inventory management, shipping calculation, invoicing, payment reconciliation, customer accounts or returns management.

### Can a D2C brand use WhatsApp catalog without a website?

Yes. A brand can receive orders manually through WhatsApp and use UPI, payment links or cash on delivery, depending on its process. However, a website becomes useful as the product range, order volume and need for automated checkout increase.

### Does WhatsApp catalog automatically update stock?

Not necessarily. Stock synchronisation depends on the tools and integrations used. If the catalog is managed manually, the team must update availability and should confirm stock before accepting payment.

### Can customers pay directly inside WhatsApp?

Payment features and availability can vary by account, location and current WhatsApp or Meta functionality. Many Indian businesses use a payment gateway link, UPI or website checkout shared through WhatsApp. Test the complete payment and order confirmation process before promoting it widely.

### How many products should a new D2C brand add?

There is no fixed ideal number. Begin with a focused range that is in stock, clearly described and operationally easy to fulfil. A smaller, accurate catalog is usually more useful than a larger catalog containing outdated products or incomplete details.

### Do WhatsApp catalog products need GST prices?

The catalog should communicate pricing accurately and avoid confusion about taxes. Whether GST applies and how it should be shown depends on your registration and transaction structure. Confirm the correct treatment and invoice format with your tax adviser.

## Where to Start

Begin with five practical steps:

1. Choose a dedicated WhatsApp Business number and complete the business profile.
2. Select the initial products that are available and easy to fulfil.
3. Prepare a product sheet with names, prices, images, variants, SKUs, links and policies.
4. Decide whether orders will be handled manually, through a website or through an integrated system.
5. Test the complete journey from catalog view to payment, invoice, dispatch and support.

Keep the first version focused. Once the process works, add collections, saved replies, tracking integrations and automation based on actual customer questions.
